When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents

Researchers introduced MERIT, a new benchmark that evaluates how long-term memory affects task-executing LLM agents under strict cost and token accounting. The study found that using memory dramatically increases task success—raising it from a baseline of 0.00 up to 1.00—though swapping memory implementations can alter success rates by up to 60 points. Furthermore, update-on-write memory systems significantly outperformed embedding retrieval when handling updated facts, while full dialogue replay was proven to never be economically viable.

Safety for Whom? Refusing the Right Subset of a Topic, Not the Whole Topic

Current AI safety guardrails often over-refuse user prompts by completely blocking broad, sensitive subjects instead of targeting genuinely harmful requests. The article advocates for a more nuanced approach that selectively refuses only the dangerous subsets of a topic. This targeted strategy aims to balance safety with usefulness, ensuring AI models remain helpful for benign queries without compromising on real risks.

OpenAI fought dirty on career-making math problem, says NYU mathematician

An NYU mathematician claims that OpenAI 'fought dirty' regarding a high-stakes, career-making math problem. The issue involves the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, which offers a $1 million bounty for the first person to provide a solution.

Meta debuts its Muse AI agent. Will consumers trust it?

Meta has launched 'Muse,' a new personal AI agent that marks the company's largest consumer AI initiative to date. The tool requires extensive access to sensitive user data, including emails, calendars, payments, and health records. Ultimately, the rollout serves as a major test of whether consumers trust Meta enough to grant it access to their private information.

Hackers are stealing Claude tokens from subscribers

Anthropic has warned subscribers that hackers are actively stealing Claude tokens from user accounts. The issue came to light after a subscriber discovered unauthorized token consumption while they were not using the service.

Google Cloud races to catch up in the AI deployment wars with Accenture deal

To catch up in the enterprise AI market, Google Cloud is expanding its partnership with Accenture to accelerate technology adoption. The collaboration will rely on forward-deployed engineers to help businesses overcome implementation bottlenecks and efficiently integrate AI solutions.

Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers

This paper introduces a damage-aware multi-armed bandit framework to improve structured post-training pruning for vision and language transformers. By evaluating 'paired damage' (masked loss minus base loss) on calibration batches, the method sequentially identifies and zeroes out attention heads and MLP channels with minimal performance loss. Experiments across a wide range of models demonstrate that this approach consistently reduces performance degradation compared to traditional pruning baselines under a fixed evaluation budget.

CriticGen: Generation-Aware Evaluation as Actionable Feedback

Researchers have introduced CriticGen, a generation-aware framework designed to provide fine-grained, actionable feedback for evaluating and improving large language models. By dynamically creating instance-specific rubrics, CriticGen enables models to diagnose flaws and jointly produce scores, explanations, executable suggestions, and refined answers. In experiments, the framework achieved strong score correlations and successfully improved over 73% of model responses with a 93.28% non-degradation rate.

Cognition hits $48B valuation, signaling investors believe AI coding is far from a winner-take-all market

Cognition has achieved a $48 billion valuation, signaling that investors believe the AI coding industry is far from a winner-take-all market. Additionally, Cognition's valuation multiple is higher than Cursor's was prior to Cursor being sold to SpaceX.

Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models

To evaluate how Large Language Models (LLMs) understand 'metanorms'—the social expectations governing how humans react to rule violations—researchers introduced a new benchmark dataset and evaluation framework called NormReact. The study reveals that current LLMs significantly overpredict harsh punishments and negative sanctions compared to actual human judgment. Consequently, current AI systems risk providing a distorted view of social regulation by over-representing punitive responses and under-representing real-world human tolerance and restraint.

AutoFyn Technical Report: Non-Parametric Expert Iteration for Long-Horizon Agents

**AutoFyn** introduces a novel agent framework that enhances frozen AI models over long-horizon tasks by updating persistent state—such as memory files and reports—rather than modifying model weights. The system employs an orchestrator to explore multiple solutions and a verifier to score progress, distilling verified feedback back into the durable state to guide subsequent rounds. Demonstrated across mathematics, data science, and cybersecurity, AutoFyn outperformed default coding agents on IMO problems, topped the Spider 2.0 benchmark, and discovered 16 maintainer-confirmed software vulnerabilities.

AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome

The AlphaGenome Atlas provides a predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome. Through this resource, it details the molecular effects of 9 billion single-letter DNA variants.

Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know

The rapid rise of artificial intelligence has generated a vast amount of new technical terms and industry slang. To help readers navigate this evolving vocabulary, the article provides a glossary defining some of the most essential AI words and phrases.

Travis Kalanick’s Atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business

Uber founder Travis Kalanick appears to be positioning his latest venture, Atoms, to enter the robotaxi industry. Kalanick stated that this move will allow him to address 'unfinished business,' hinting at a return to the autonomous vehicle ambitions he originally pursued during his time at Uber.

Iris: Climbing to the Search Frontier

Researchers have introduced Iris-mini and Iris-pro, two search agents trained using a multi-hop web data pipeline and an alternating 'SFT-RL climbing' procedure optimized against live search. Evaluated with inference-time context management, both models achieved the strongest overall results among open-source search agents in their parameter classes across benchmarks such as BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and HLE. The authors plan to publicly release the model weights alongside the complete data construction, training, and evaluation recipes.

Harbor Adapters and Harbor-Index: Infrastructure and a Curated Meta-Dataset for Large-Scale Agentic Evaluation

To simplify agentic evaluation across complex environments, researchers developed Harbor Adapters, an open-source infrastructure that adapts over 80 benchmarks for testing arbitrary AI agents. Using this platform, the authors conducted a large-scale evaluation of eight models across 54 benchmarks and introduced Harbor-Index, a curated and affordable meta-dataset of 82 challenging tasks from 29 benchmarks. Across all evaluated model-harness configurations on Harbor-Index, no model exceeded a 30% pass rate, demonstrating the suite's high difficulty and effectiveness for testing agent capabilities.

From Matching Models to Recruiting Agents: A Systematized Narrative Review of AI Recruitment Systems, Evaluation, and Governance

This systematized narrative review traces the evolution of AI recruitment systems from basic profile-matching models to multi-stage workflows and tool-using recruiting agents. Based on an analysis of 40 representative works, the study highlights critical gaps, such as reliance on private data, hidden pipeline failures, and a complete lack of joint evaluations covering utility, fairness, privacy, and security. To address these limitations, the authors introduce a staged evaluation framework and an agenda for auditable, evidence-grounded recruitment systems governed by explicit cost and risk constraints.

EXAONE Forecast for Finance

**EXAONE Forecast for Finance** is a new time series foundation model specifically designed to address the computational and missing-data challenges inherent to financial forecasting. By replacing heavy self-attention mechanisms with efficient linear-time operators and pretraining on a massive multi-asset dataset, the model effectively captures complex market dynamics. Consequently, EXAONE Finance achieved state-of-the-art performance on the FinVerse benchmark, ranking first in point-forecast accuracy, cross-sectional asset ranking, and portfolio profitability.

Data-Optimized Contingency Screening: A Machine Learning Approach to Power System Security

Researchers have developed a machine learning framework using Random Forest, SVM, and KNN algorithms to classify power system contingencies into safe, moderate, or severe risk levels to prevent grid failures. By combining these models with pre-processing techniques like PCA and SMOTE, Random Forest achieved the highest performance with F1 scores up to 0.97, with PCA contributing the most to model accuracy. Ultimately, the study highlights machine learning as a scalable and powerful alternative to traditional contingency analysis for real-time power system security assessment.

Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement

Authors are disputing the distribution of funds from a recent copyright settlement with the AI company Anthropic. They contend that publishers and literary agents are attempting to claim an unfairly large portion of the payout. As a result, creators are pushing back to ensure they receive proper compensation for the use of their work.

Training a coding model to paint watercolours with TRL and OpenEnv

Based on the provided title, the article describes a method for training a coding AI model to paint watercolours. This training process is implemented using the TRL and OpenEnv frameworks.

Real-Time Intelligence with IBM Time Series Models on Confluent

IBM has integrated its AI-driven time series models with Confluent's data streaming platform to enable real-time predictive analytics. This collaboration allows businesses to continuously analyze live sequential data streams to generate immediate, actionable intelligence. By unifying real-time data infrastructure with advanced forecasting, organizations can significantly improve automated decision-making for operations, demand planning, and risk management.

This article focuses on equipping AI coding agents with a dedicated memory system. It emphasizes the importance of users maintaining direct ownership and control over the memory utilized by these agents.

Fine-tuning a 350M Model for Better Structured Outputs in 100 GRPO Steps

This article highlights a method for fine-tuning a compact 350-million parameter AI model to significantly improve its ability to generate reliable, structured outputs. By utilizing Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), the model achieved enhanced performance in remarkably few training iterations—just 100 steps. This demonstrates a highly efficient, low-resource approach for optimizing smaller models for specialized formatting tasks.

docs.title: LLM-Augmented Causal Discovery: Probabilistic Fusion of Edge Existence and Orientation
docs.text:
Researchers have proposed a novel approach called Probabilistic Dependency Graphs (PDGs) to improve causal discovery by combining traditional Bayesian network structure learning (BNSL) with large language models (LLMs). This method represents edge existence and directionality from both sources as probability distributions, allowing their outputs to be merged via weighted averaging. Extensive benchmarking across 26 networks using major LLMs—including Gemini, Claude, and GPT—showed that a simple 50/50 fusion outperformed either source operating independently in 22 of the test cases. The performance boost occurs because BNSL excels at discovering where edge connections exist, whereas LLMs provide significantly higher accuracy in determining the direction of those edges. Ultimately, the key takeaways are that data-driven algorithms and LLMs play highly complementary roles in causal inference, and fusing their outputs into a shared probabilistic framework offers a practical, statistically significant improvement to causal graph accuracy.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Not All Explanations Are Sought: Information-Seeking Psychology for Human-Centered XAI
docs.text:
A recent position paper argues that Human-Centered Explainable AI (HCXAI) needs to integrate the psychology of information-seeking to design better user interactions. According to the authors, people evaluate whether to engage with AI explanations based on expected instrumental, hedonic, and cognitive utility. However, common cognitive biases often distort these utility evaluations, leading users to either consume excessive explanations that fragment attention or ignore vital risk information entirely. This dilemma is particularly pressing for agentic AI systems, where human oversight requires anticipating complex, cascading autonomous actions. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that AI developers must move beyond simply making explanations available and instead design systems grounded in human psychology that motivate users to actively seek and effectively use explanations.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Rating the Raters: Rasch Measurement Theory for LLM Evaluation
docs.text:
A new research paper proposes using Rasch Measurement Theory (RMT) to address critical limitations in current Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation methods. While standard practices often fail to isolate how specific test items and raters influence scores, RMT separates these variables onto a unified scale to detect miscalibrations and biases. To test the framework, researchers analyzed annotations from nine different LLMs evaluating a hate speech dataset. The analysis revealed that LLMs systematically diverge from human annotators in scoring severity, question-order sensitivity, target identity bias, and overall scale usage. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that conventional metrics hide significant model biases, making Rasch Measurement Theory an essential tool for accurately evaluating LLMs whether they act as examinees, judges, or content raters.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Retrieving Relations, Detecting Fallacies: A RAG Approach to Political Debate Analysis
docs.text:
Detecting fallacious arguments in political debates is crucial for public discourse, yet automatic identification requires complex contextual and relational knowledge beyond simple text analysis. To overcome the limitations of traditional static classifiers, researchers developed a novel framework that dynamically retrieves relevant context using argumentative relations such as support and attack. The methodology was evaluated on the ElecDeb60to20 benchmark across 14 distinct models, leveraging a 15GB political knowledge base. Experimental results showed substantial performance improvements over non-retrieval baselines, reaching macro-F1 scores of up to 0.864 for fallacy detection and 0.725 for classification. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that dynamically incorporating external knowledge through argumentatively guided retrieval significantly enhances an AI system's ability to accurately identify and categorize logical fallacies in political discourse.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
docs.text:
Apple has uncovered what it describes as "shocking evidence" against a former employee accused of stealing proprietary company data to benefit OpenAI. The tech giant alleges that the worker exfiltrated sensitive trade secrets and confidential information prior to leaving his role. Furthermore, Apple revealed that the individual deliberately attempted to cover his tracks by destroying evidence of the data theft upon learning he was under investigation. This alleged obstruction has significantly escalated the legal dispute, shedding light on the aggressive measures companies are taking to protect their internal developments. Ultimately, the key takeaways from this case highlight the escalating battle for AI dominance, the growing threat of insider intellectual property theft, and the severe legal consequences of attempting to destroy digital evidence.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Benchmarking General Mobile Assistants in Challenging Real-World Scenarios
docs.text:
A new benchmark called GMA (General Mobile Assistants) has been developed to evaluate autonomous AI agents across diverse, complex mobile environments that existing benchmarks fail to capture. Built around seven open-source applications, GMA introduces 300 tasks across four difficulty tiers, ranging from basic atomic actions to intricate multi-step workflows. When researchers evaluated eight leading frontier models, they found that AI performance declined significantly as task difficulty increased, proving that current agents are not yet ready to reliably handle realistic user needs. The study also demonstrated that optimizing an agent's harness design—such as implementing explicit state tracking and context retention—can meaningfully boost performance on complex workflows. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that while current mobile AI agents fall far short of real-world reliability, GMA offers a vital testbed showing that thoughtful harness engineering is essential to closing this capability gap.

Read the full article →

docs.title: CareGraph: An Auditable Hybrid AI Framework for Evidence-Grounded Personalized Longitudinal Health Intelligence
docs.text:
Researchers have developed CareGraph, an auditable hybrid AI framework designed to convert fragmented clinical, wearable, and self-reported patient data into structured, traceable health insights. Built with strict safety controls, the framework deliberately avoids autonomous diagnosis or treatment selection, focusing instead on identifying trends, missing context indicators, and bounded next steps. In synthetic cohort evaluations, CareGraph demonstrated high performance in trend analysis and significantly improved missing context detection compared to legacy systems. Furthermore, when benchmarked against monolithic GPT-5.6, CareGraph generated faster and more concise syntheses while offering deterministic retrieval and graph-verified provenance. Ultimately, CareGraph demonstrates that combining graph auditing with constrained language models provides a faster, safer, and fully auditable foundation for personalized health intelligence than monolithic AI models.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Class-Based Heuristic Selection for Solving the Flying Block Puzzle
docs.text:
Standard heuristic search algorithms often fail in complex, constrained spatial environments like robotic navigation and warehouse logistics. To address this issue, researchers introduced the Class-Based Heuristic A (CBHA) algorithm, evaluating it on the NP-complete Flying Block Puzzle microworld designed to mirror real-world spatial bottlenecks. CBHA improves search efficiency by partitioning the state space into seven distinct structural classes, applying provably admissible class-specific heuristics, and dynamically adjusting tie-breaking rules. Tested across 146 benchmark instances, CBHA achieved a 93.4% success rate while reducing search node expansions by nearly 88% relative to standard A* search. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that class-triggered adaptive heuristics provide a highly efficient, principled mechanism for spatial AI planning that successfully generalizes to complex physical constraint systems.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M
docs.text:
Three-year-old startup Clipto utilizes artificial intelligence to enable users to efficiently search through terabytes of video data. Demonstrating remarkably swift commercial traction, the company successfully scaled its business to reach $15 million in annual recurring revenue. Furthermore, Clipto managed to achieve profitability before seeking any additional outside capital. To support its continued growth, the company recently secured a fresh $15 million funding round. Ultimately, reaching a $250 million valuation while maintaining profitability demonstrates the immense market demand and strong investor confidence in AI-driven video search technologies.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Context Localization for Generalized Level-Based Evaluation in Knowledge-Based Systems
docs.text:
A recent study proposes a mathematical framework for context localization in knowledge-based systems to improve generalized level-based evaluations. The approach models scenarios where structured, nonnegative scores assigned to facts, rules, or evidence units are evaluated using conditional aggregation tests across admissible contexts. The primary theoretical result proves that filtering scores by a target context aligns with localizing those contexts if and only if two conditions are met: context monotonicity and a reduction property that eliminates external localized support. Furthermore, the researchers extended this consistency analysis to block-generated mechanisms and parameterized systems. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that this framework establishes a vital stability criterion for reliable, context-dependent evidence selection and non-additive knowledge aggregation in artificial intelligence systems.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Effectiveness of IoT and Deep Learning for Detection and Severity Assessment of Postelectrotermes militaris in Tea Plantations
docs.text:
Researchers have introduced an innovative IoT and deep-learning framework designed to detect and assess Upcountry Live Wood Termite infestations in tea plantations. The non-invasive system utilizes Raspberry Pi-connected microphones to capture tree trunk audio, transforming the sound data into spectrograms for analysis. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) classifies whether a tree is infested, while a secondary model evaluates infestation severity by incorporating audio amplitude and geospatial proximity to nearby affected plants. During field trials conducted under realistic environmental noise conditions, the AI model demonstrated solid performance, achieving an 81.5% accuracy rate on the test data. The key takeaway is that this technology effectively combines acoustic AI detection with geospatial mapping, empowering plantation managers to identify high-risk areas early, prioritize field inspections, and implement targeted pest control measures.

Read the full article →

docs.title: From Atari to EVE Online: Building on 15 Years of AI Research in Games
docs.text:
For over fifteen years, Google DeepMind has used video games as a primary benchmark for artificial intelligence, progressing from mastering retro Atari classics to navigating complex, player-driven worlds like EVE Online. This historical evolution enabled researchers to advance machine learning from simple reflex-based actions toward sophisticated long-term strategy and multi-agent cooperation. Moving beyond pure research, DeepMind is now actively partnering with game studios to bring these advanced models directly into game production. Through these collaborations, developers and researchers are prototyping groundbreaking gameplay features, including highly adaptive non-player characters and dynamic, evolving environments. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that fifteen years of foundational AI research in games is now successfully transitioning into practical development, promising to revolutionize interactive game design and create richer player experiences.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash lets you build with more control
docs.text:
Google has announced Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, an upgraded lightweight AI model designed for high-speed performance and minimal latency. This release grants developers significantly more control through expanded parameters for system instructions, precise output formatting, and granular safety controls. Despite its streamlined footprint, the model preserves powerful multimodal capabilities across text, audio, and visual data streams. Improved API infrastructure further simplifies enterprise integration, facilitating seamless deployment into live software environments. Key Takeaways: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash delivers a faster, cheaper, and highly customizable AI model that empowers developers to build precise, real-time multimodal applications at scale.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Granite 4.2 LLMs: How They're Built
docs.text:
IBM's Granite 4.2 large language models (LLMs) represent a targeted approach to building high-performance, open-source AI tailored for enterprise applications. The development process relies on meticulously curated datasets that focus heavily on programming code, mathematical reasoning, and domain-specific business data. To maximize performance while controlling operational costs, the engineering team utilized efficient Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures paired with IBM's InstructLab alignment methodology. Furthermore, robust data filtering and safety guardrails were embedded directly into the training pipeline to mitigate copyright risks and harmful outputs. Ultimately, the key takeaways of Granite 4.2 are its open-source accessibility, computational efficiency, and enterprise-first design that combines top-tier performance with strict safety and compliance standards.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a ‘Harvey for police officers’
docs.text:
Blue Voice, a startup founded by a Harvard Law dropout, has successfully raised $6 million in funding to build an artificial intelligence tool tailored for law enforcement. Described as a "Harvey for police officers," the platform aims to provide specialized digital support during daily police operations. Unlike general-purpose AI systems, Blue Voice relies on localized datasets, including department-specific laws, local ordinances, and internal operational protocols. Because these specialized guidelines contain proprietary information, standard AI tools cannot access them on the public internet. In summary, the key takeaway is that Blue Voice is utilizing its $6 million funding to fill a critical gap in public safety technology by delivering a specialized AI assistant trained on exclusive, non-public law enforcement data.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Hypothesize, Evaluate, Refine: A Scientific Agent for PDE Discovery with Unknown Spatial Coefficient Fields
docs.text:
Researchers have presented HER-PDE, a scientific-agent framework designed to discover governing partial differential equation (PDE) structures alongside unknown spatial coefficient fields. To address the challenge of coupled PDE operators and spatial fields, the agent analyzes noisy trajectories from different excitations to form and refine expression-tree hypotheses. The framework evaluates these structures using bidirectional cross-excitation transfer and subsequently audits the selected governing law on a sealed temporal interval. When tested on five two-dimensional systems with five percent relative Gaussian state noise, the agent successfully recovered the exact generating operator in all five cases. Ultimately, the key takeaways demonstrate that this agent-guided refinement process can successfully recover heterogeneous governing laws without prescribing a parametric form for their spatial coefficients, achieving a median Pearson correlation of approximately 0.85 across nine unknown fields.

Read the full article →

docs.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
docs.text:

The process reduces large neural network models to a highly efficient 4-bit architecture, drastically cutting memory usage and computational demands. Unlike standard quantization methods that typically degrade accuracy, QAH applies targeted fine-tuning to actively repair the performance loss introduced during the compression stage. Remarkably, the resulting 4-bit model not only retains its capabilities, but actually surpasses the accuracy and overall performance of its original, full-precision baseline. The key takeaway is that Quantization-Aware Healing proves AI models can be drastically compressed for faster, cheaper deployment while simultaneously achieving superior performance over their uncompressed predecessors.

docs.title: BenchMIRT: What are LLM benchmarks actually measuring?
docs.text:
A new study introduces BenchMIRT, a framework designed to critically analyze what popular Large Language Model (LLM) benchmarks are actually measuring. By applying Multidimensional Item Response Theory from psychometrics, the researchers evaluated how effectively standard test questions differentiate between distinct model capabilities. The analysis revealed that many popular AI benchmarks contain significant question redundancy, inconsistent difficulty scaling, and often conflate simple memorization with complex reasoning. Consequently, high performance on existing leaderboards does not always correlate with genuine intelligence or real-world utility. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that current LLM benchmarks are frequently flawed and imprecise, highlighting the critical need for psychometrically grounded frameworks like BenchMIRT to establish more accurate, trustworthy AI evaluation standards.

docs.title: Discrete-Time MDP Modeling for Multi-Item Capacitated Lot Sizing with Stochastic Demand Timing
docs.text:
This paper addresses a finite-horizon multi-item capacitated lot-sizing problem characterized by deterministic demand quantities but uncertain arrival timing. To capture capacity competition, backlogs, and dynamic inventory allocations under this uncertainty, the authors formulate the problem as a discrete-time Markov decision process (DTMDP). Their analysis reveals that stochastic demand timing drastically expands the state space, memory demands, and solution times compared to deterministic baselines. To solve large instances efficiently, the researchers introduced a Genetic Algorithm (GA) that searches over feasible state-feedback policies and evaluates them directly within the DTMDP framework. Key Takeaways: Across 330 benchmark instances, the proposed Genetic Algorithm demonstrated near-optimal performance with an average optimality gap of just 3.44%, while achieving an average 6.89-fold computational speedup on difficult instances where exact methods encounter severe hardware limitations.

docs.title: HyperWorld: Hypergraph-Structured State Serialization Improves Learned Textual World Models
docs.text:
A new study introduces HyperWorld, a framework designed to evaluate how different state serialization structures impact the performance of learned textual world models in AI agents. Researchers compared raw text observations against three symbolic state representations: independent sentences, pairwise triples, and entity-centered hyperedges that group related facts. Across various tests, hyperedge serialization consistently demonstrated superior results for small-to-medium-sized models ranging from 0.5B to 1.5B parameters. Furthermore, the hyperedge representation achieved the highest overall success rate during downstream planning tasks compared to the other tested formats. Ultimately, the key takeaways are that higher-order hypergraph state organization serves as a simple yet powerful inductive bias for textual world models, providing the most significant benefits when model capacity is restricted or when agents operate in novel, out-of-distribution environments.

docs.title: I-CARE: Analysis of interference-related phenomena in a controllable, diverse and representative unlearning setting for text-to-image models
docs.text:
Machine unlearning aims to remove specific knowledge from AI models, but it often leads to "interference," where unintended degradation occurs to semantically related concepts that should be retained. To address the poor characterization and inconsistent evaluation of this problem in text-to-image models, researchers introduced a new methodology called I-CARE. Instead of introducing a transient benchmark, I-CARE establishes formal definitions, standardized metrics, and reporting templates designed to adapt as unlearning algorithms evolve. The practical viability of the framework was successfully demonstrated using state-of-the-art algorithms, and the system was released alongside an intuitive, web-based interface. Ultimately, the key takeaways are that I-CARE establishes a standardized, future-proof approach for systematically studying interference in machine unlearning while offering open-source tools that make these insights easily accessible to researchers.

docs.title: Incremental Risk Assessment of Progressive Elder Financial Scams via Instruction-Tuned Small Language Models
docs.text:
Financial scams targeting older adults typically escalate across multiple conversational turns, making early detection difficult without continuous monitoring. To combat this, researchers proposed a cumulative turn-based risk assessment framework that continuously re-evaluates scam risks at every stage of an evolving dialogue. The researchers tested this framework using a newly annotated multi-turn scam dataset to fine-tune four instruction-tuned small language models: Phi-4, LLaMA-3.2, DeepSeek-R1, and Qwen3. Among these, Phi-4 and LLaMA-3.2 performed exceptionally well at recognizing fraud cues and cross-turn escalation patterns relative to their parameter size. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that combining structured cumulative modeling with compact language models offers a powerful, privacy-aware solution for real-time, on-device fraud protection on resource-constrained mobile devices.

docs.title: Long-Horizon State Tracking in LLMs: Executing MD5 through a Deep Sequence of Dependent Tool Calls
docs.text:
A recent study investigates why large language models (LLMs) struggle with long-horizon tasks, where minor per-step errors typically accumulate and cause total task failure. To cleanly isolate state-tracking performance from instruction interpretation, researchers tasked an LLM with manually computing an MD5 cryptographic hash through a deep sequence of 196 dependent tool calls. The open-weights model gpt-oss-120b successfully maintained the 32-bit intermediate state across all steps and produced the exact correct hash in a majority of completed runs. This level of precision was sustained even in a multi-LLM setup operating without exact-arithmetic software, relying instead on context retention and majority voting to fix computational slips. The key takeaway is that LLMs are capable of precise, long-horizon state tracking without inevitable error decay, provided their reasoning is preserved in context and voting mechanisms are applied to eliminate step-level mistakes.
